findings.evidence: Common.lean:186-189 witness is `⟨subOfLe D (inf D E) (inf_le_left D E), by rw [coe_subOfLe]⟩`; `subOfLe` at FixedDegreeSubtraction.lean:44 yields index `e - d`.
findings.fix: Define `leftResidual D E := subOfLe D (inf D E) (inf_le_left D E)` (and symmetrically for `rightResidual`); drop `exists_leftResidual`/`exists_rightResidual`. Then `coe_leftResidual` becomes `coe_subOfLe` (rfl).
findings.issue: `leftResidual`/`rightResidual` are `Classical.choose` renamings of `subOfLe D (inf D E) (inf_le_left D E)` / `subOfLe E (inf D E) (inf_le_right D E)`; the witness in `exists_leftResidual` (line 187) is exactly that term and already has the declared degree index `d - (degree (D ⊓ E)).toNat`, so the existential scaffolding adds nothing.

findings.evidence: Existing `multiplicityFinsupp_subOfLe D E hED : (subOfLe D E hED).multiplicityFinsupp = D.multiplicityFinsupp - E.multiplicityFinsupp` at FixedDegreeSubtraction.lean:70.
findings.fix: With the definition above, obtain these from `multiplicityFinsupp_subOfLe` combined with `multiplicityFinsupp_inf`, deleting the manual proofs.
findings.issue: `multiplicityFinsupp_leftResidual`/`_rightResidual` re-prove (16 lines of `toNat`/omega) exactly `multiplicityFinsupp_subOfLe` specialized to the subtrahend `inf D E`.

findings.evidence: `equivSym_subOfLe` at FixedDegreeSubtraction.lean:97 has the same statement shape and proof.
findings.fix: Derive from `equivSym_subOfLe` after redefining the residuals via `subOfLe`.
findings.issue: `equivSym_leftResidual`/`_rightResidual` clone `equivSym_subOfLe` (identical `equivSym_apply; congr 1; ext x; simp` shape).

findings.evidence: `add_subOfLe` (FixedDegreeSubtraction.lean:120) and `subOfLe_add` (:131) give the same reconstruction-up-to-cast statements.
findings.fix: Reduce these to `subOfLe_add`/`add_subOfLe` once the residuals are `subOfLe` applications.
findings.issue: `leftResidual_add_inf`/`inf_add_leftResidual` (and right variants at 274/286) restate `subOfLe_add`/`add_subOfLe` with `E := inf D E`.

summary: The common-part API (`inf` and its lemmas) is genuinely new, but the residual half wraps the existing `subOfLe` in `Classical.choose` and re-derives the whole `subOfLe` lemma set instead of reusing it.
